passages.note: Bill details page naming Bascom as author; it prints the digest, not the enacted provision.

passages.provision_quote: If a law enforcement officer arrests an individual for a felony or a misdemeanor and there is probable cause to believe that the person is not lawfully present in the United States, the jail or detention facility shall, during the intake process at the jail or detention facility, notify the county sheriff of the probable cause to believe the person is not lawfully present in the United States.
passages.note: Enrolled text of the bill Bascom authored; it sets a notification duty and names no one who is to be removed.

rows.reasoning: Bascom authored HB 1393 (2025), whose operative section requires that a jail "notify the county sheriff of the probable cause to believe the person is not lawfully present in the United States" and that the sheriff "report information received under subsection (b) to the proper authority". That is a law requiring state and local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, which the annex places on the local-immigration question: it does not say whether the government should "Stop deportations entirely", deport "only ... undocumented immigrants convicted of serious violent crimes", or "Deport all undocumented immigrants". Both passages are adjacent, so nothing survives to seat a chair.
needs_source: Bascom's own words on how far the government should go in deporting undocumented immigrants (floor statement, questionnaire, or first-person issue page)
